notes: Direct HTTP fetch of ikea.com/in/en/ throughout (HTTP 200, no blocking, robots.txt 404 so no Claude-specific disallow to worry about) -- re-derived independently from India's own homepage mega-menu JSON and category pages, not copied from the other IKEA-market archives. Homepage embedded categorisation JSON has a single top-level 'Pet products' node (id pt001, url /in/en/cat/pet-products-pt001/) under the Products root, with exactly two subs: 'Cat products' (39569) and 'Dog products' (39570). Fetched pt001 directly: it is a pure grouping/hub page (no plp-filter-information__total-count block present at all, i.e. no directly-assigned products of its own -- confirmed by absence of the total-count marker on that page while it IS present on both child pages), so recorded as is_group. Fetched both leaf pages and cross-checked two independent signals on each, matching exactly: (1) the SSR-rendered 'plp-filter-information__total-count' header text, (2) the bottom-of-page 'Showing N of N results' text plus its <progress value=N max=N> attributes. Cat products: 5 items / Showing 5 of 5 / max=5 (all three agree). Dog products: 6 items / Showing 6 of 6 / max=6 (all three agree). Product alt-text on both pages confirms genuine pet-care items under IKEA's UTSADD range (pet beds, pet cushions, pet bowls, dog toy, dog bed) -- not pet-themed decor. Searched the full homepage categorisation JSON (which lists every top-level and nested category name site-wide) for litter/scratch/leash/collar/kennel/crate/paw/cat food/dog food/treat -- zero additional hits beyond 'Pet products' itself, and neither leaf page's subCategories array has any children (both are terminal leaves: subCategories:[]). No cat litter, carriers, leashes, crates, training, or grooming lines found anywhere on the India site outside this single pt001 hub -- IKEA India's pet range is limited to the two UTSADD leaf categories. Site's own /search/?q=pet%20care page is client-rendered (empty in raw HTML) so was not usable as a discovery signal; relied on the homepage mega-menu JSON and direct category-page fetches instead, per the absence-proof requirement to check real navigation/category tree rather than site search alone.
